summary: Resubmitted update.json with one recorded change instead of repeating it verbatim: the primary interpretation's limitations now carry the source-anchor audit I ran this turn. All 24 declared sources were re-read from the captured tree and each still lands on the code or text it is cited for — the scan and its max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1 bound (api.go 601-622), restoreFromCommittedLogs raising lastApplied to the commit-tracking store's index (api.go 723-755), the snapshot-configuration restore (api.go 645-689), processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623), the skipped membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784), configuration-change admission and commit-on-append (raft.go 1204-1241, 1236-1241), nextConfiguration (configuration.go 224-302), the verifyLeader quorum (raft.go 964-988), the two repair-by-installation anchors (raft.go 1953-1961, 1569-1578), the bootstrap refusal and RecoverCluster (api.go 260-267, 321-448), and the snapshot trigger with the user-restore hole (replication.go 222-224, raft.go 1097-1199). No anchor was off by a line or attached to a different construct, so the audit produced no correction; it is recorded because every claim in the account rests on those ranges having been read in the captured tree. Nothing else in the file changed: no new experiments or receipts, and the finding itself stands exactly as previously validated — the measured trigger is the persisted commit index at or above the newest configuration entry (656e33fb90f24c58a94928eeeeb938aa and its repeat 202311f4911e4af5828d49134f37811c), with the empty-configuration, stale-membership, resurrected-voter, forgotten-added-voter, client-contract and operator-recovery consequences each receipt-backed with controls and repeats. The two known blemishes remain documented rather than rewritten: the earlier over-broad repair claim and the stored repair Fact's shortened evidence list.
